sample_tweets.text: It feels like vendors keep repeating that defensive AI agents will stop offensive AI agents until everyone accepts it without evidence.  Solo hackers were ransoming fortune 500 organizations which had entire dedicated SOC teams. How does giving both sides AI somehow lead to defenders winning?  It reminds me of when NextGen Firewalls hit the market. Organizations were falling over themselves to buy the fancy magic box with blinky lights that solves all their security problems.  Then, ironically, not only did the magic boxes not solve all their security problems, hackers figured out that the firewalls run outdated Linux kernels with exploit mitigations disabled, so they just hacked those too.

There's genuinely so much runtime exploit mitigation potential with eBPF, but the last thing you want is AI Agents writing rules that impact your kernel. Also, the capabilities are limited to Linux because Mac/Windows haven't implement the components needed to be effective.
